name: Modular Cabin Kitchen
short_description: Pre-built kitchen units craned into position — the workhorse of commercial temporary catering.
long_description: Modular cabin kitchens are the most common type of commercial temporary kitchen. They arrive as pre-built, fully equipped units that are craned into position on site. Available in 20ft and 28ft configurations, they can serve anywhere from 200 to 800+ meals per day. Multiple units can be linked together for larger operations. They require a firm, level surface and crane access for delivery. Typical setup includes full cooking lines, extraction, refrigeration, and hot/cold running water.

name: Trailer Kitchen
short_description: Towable kitchen units that can be repositioned easily — ideal for events and multi-site operations.
long_description: Trailer kitchens are fully self-contained cooking facilities built onto a towable chassis. They can be moved between sites without a crane, making them popular for events, festivals, and organisations that need flexibility. Available in various sizes, they typically include full cooking equipment, extraction systems, and can connect to mains utilities or run from generators. Some providers offer rent-to-buy options on trailer kitchens.

name: Container Kitchen
short_description: Shipping container conversions that work off-grid — fully self-contained with their own power and water.
long_description: Container kitchens are converted shipping containers (typically 20ft or 40ft) fitted out as complete commercial kitchens. Their key advantage is self-containment — many can operate entirely off-grid with built-in generators, water tanks, and waste systems. This makes them ideal for remote locations, construction sites, and emergency deployments. They are extremely durable and weather-resistant. Some specialist providers offer fire-rated versions for high-risk town centre locations.

name: Lorry Kitchen
short_description: Full-scale kitchens built into 40ft lorry trailers — maximum capacity for large-scale operations.
long_description: Lorry kitchens are the largest mobile kitchen option, built into 40ft articulated trailers. They provide maximum cooking capacity and are typically used for very large events, military operations, disaster relief, or major construction projects. They arrive and depart under their own power (with a tractor unit) so require no crane. However, they need significant space and level ground for setup.

name: Marquee Kitchen
short_description: Temporary kitchen facilities within marquee structures — flexible sizing for events of any scale.
long_description: Marquee kitchens use commercial-grade marquee structures fitted out with professional kitchen equipment. They offer the most flexibility in terms of size and layout, as they can be configured to almost any specification. They are commonly used for outdoor events, weddings, festivals, and as temporary extensions to existing kitchen facilities. They require flat ground and are weather-dependent, though modern marquees handle most UK conditions.

name: Flat Pack Kitchen
short_description: Modular panels that walk through standard doorways — perfect when crane access is impossible.
long_description: Flat pack kitchens are designed to be carried through standard doorways, corridors, and lifts in individual panels, then assembled on site. This solves the critical access problem that prevents crane-delivered units from reaching many locations — particularly in city centres, inside buildings, or in areas with restricted access. Once assembled, they provide the same functionality as a modular cabin kitchen. Assembly typically takes 1-2 days.

name: Driveway Pod — Large
short_description: A fully equipped kitchen delivered to your driveway — everything you need while your kitchen is being renovated.
long_description: Large driveway pods are the most popular domestic temporary kitchen option. They are delivered on the back of a lorry and placed on your driveway or garden. Inside, you get a full-size fridge-freezer, microwave, oven or hob, kettle, toaster, sink with hot and cold water, worktop space, and storage. They connect to your home's electricity and water supply. Most families find they can cook completely normal meals. Typical hire periods are 4-12 weeks during kitchen renovations.

name: Driveway Pod — Compact
short_description: A smaller kitchen pod for tighter spaces — all essential appliances in a compact footprint.
long_description: Compact driveway pods offer the same functionality as their larger counterparts but in a smaller footprint. They are designed for homes with limited driveway space, narrow access, or smaller households. They typically include a microwave, mini fridge, kettle, toaster, sink, and worktop. They are lighter and easier to manoeuvre into position, and some can fit through standard garden gates.

name: Indoor Capsule Kitchen
short_description: A pop-up kitchen installed inside your home — no driveway needed, no going outside in the rain.
long_description: Indoor capsule kitchens are a unique domestic solution that installs inside your home — typically in a living room, dining room, or spare bedroom. They are designed to be carried through your front door and assembled in under 2 hours. This solves the key problem of driveway pods: you don't need a driveway, you don't need to go outside to cook, and they work perfectly in flats and apartments. They include a microwave, mini fridge, kettle, toaster, and portable hob, with a built-in splashback and worktop.

name: Open Plan Kitchen
short_description: Olympic-scale temporary kitchen installations — bespoke builds for the largest operations on earth.
long_description: Open plan kitchens are fully bespoke, large-scale temporary kitchen installations designed for major events and operations. The most notable example is the Olympic Games, where temporary kitchen facilities serve tens of thousands of meals daily. These are engineered solutions involving multiple connected units, industrial equipment, and complex logistics. They are designed, project-managed, and installed by specialist providers with dedicated transport fleets and engineering teams.
